title: Big bag, small bag and Duke's valet Jonesy
summary: Harry Carney explained the big bag and little bag system on the road, and Procope describes valet Jonesy, a former Cotton Club bus boy, who handled bags and died of asthma.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Well, anyway, to make a story, that's the way it happened, and of course it went down and we played the six weeks at the Paramount Theater, which was real beautiful, real fine. And I remember between shows, they were getting ready to close the last week of the engagement, and I remember talking to Harry Carney, we were between shows, standing on

the sidewalk on 44th Street. I didn't even have any bags. You know, these guys, they've got their bags and they've been doing it for years.. So I said, "Well, what do you think kind of bags I should get, you know?" He said, "Well, most of the fellows have a big bag, what they call the big bag, and a small bag." That's what they called them. Oh. So I said, "Okay, I'll go buy a big bag and a small bag." So I bought a big bag and a small bag. The big bag was like a trunk, you know, and they kept that under the bus, and you carried your little bag with you, you know, with a shirt and your toothbrush and whatnot, so if you wanted to change your suit you'd go get your big bag. We had a valet, he had a valet. Duke Ellington had a famous valet named Jonesy.

Jonesy was Duke's man. Jonesy was a young fellow who Duke got from the Cotton Club. He was a bus boy up at the Cotton Club, and he got very friendly with Duke and Duke's band when they were up at the Cotton Club, and when Duke left the Cotton Club, he left and went along with Duke as, you know, a valet, a band boy or whatever. So Jonesy was along, you know, and whatever you wanted, just tell Jonesy. You'd say, "Jonesy, get my big bag." That's all you had to say and Jonesy would get your big bag and put it in the hotel lobby. You'd get a bellboy to take your big bag up to the room. Everything was beautiful. You know, you didn't have
to -- and they'd even carry your instruments for you.
That was a big band. Jonesy must have been very busy.

Jonesy? He -- I think he was an asthmatic, because I remember one night we were on this pullman train, we were on this pullman, and I came -- I woke up in the middle of the night and I climbed down out of the berth and I went in the smoker, and there was Jonesy, sitting there, gasping, and I remember taking him and opening the -- you know, those trains had dutch doors, you opened the -- and sticking his head out the window so he could get this air, you know. He sort of had an attack, you know. So it got worse and worse, you know, and he finally died from that. I don't remember exactly when he died, but he did.
